From the Sabbat Rules Update: "Members of the Sabbat antitribu clans are
outcasts, . . . they are not members of the Camarilla versions of their
clans. Cards that affect all members of a clan (such as Consanguineous
Condemnation) may affect either the Camarilla clan members or the antitribu
members, but never both."

I'm confused a bit by it as well but our play group has been considering
the antitribu as completely different clans. Therefore, any action that
affects Tremere cannot affect Tremere antitribu and vice-versa. I know that
if you look at it in RPG terms it only makes partial sense (Yes, Sabbat
Tremere would care less about letters from Vienna, but why wouldn't Gangrel
antitribu be just as susceptible to de-evolution?) but it makes things
easier to manage in V:tes, otherwise everyone would sit around trying to
figure out what cards can and cannot affect antitribu. Don't forget that
there are specific antitribu clan hosers as well, which you could not play
on their Camarilla counterparts.

Don't try to figure out cards with White Wolf game logic, I've tried to do
it and it doesn't work most of the time. Some aspects of V:tes are not
compatible with the RPG.

-- Glen McKay (Mishra Worker)

Not quite... the Antitribu are clans who have specifically turned their backs
on the Camarilla sect, and thus not only defined their own characteristic
traits, but shut themselves out of previously-accessible resources. When some
Toreador became Antitribu, they lost the ability to safely hunt in society
circles (Society Hunting Ground). So they established their own safe hunting
grounds (Fetish Club Hunting Ground). Tremere Antitribu are not affected by a
Letter From Vienna because they no longer answer to the Council of Seven. They
really don't give a flip about Etrius and his lackeys. Likewise, you may be
able to briefly twist a Malkavian into doing a task for you (Malkavian
Dementia), but don't try that silliness with the Antitribu Malkavians, their
minds operate differently. You can, however, make one paranoid enough to sit
inert for some time, until he or she takes the time to collect themselves
(Malkavian Derangement: Paranoia).

Yes, these clans are related. They decend from the same bloodlines. But the
Antitribu made a choice to follow their own paths. In many cases, this
included whole different fields of study. And while as Methuselahs we are
above such pettiness, and may control whomever we choose to focus on, we cannot
easily change the nature of Camarilla vs. Sabbat, or hope to restore basic
clan rights to an Antitribu.

Randy

>well...IMHO...thats a load of crap...this implies that the entire

>sets...and if this exclusiveness is as such, none of the cards should
>be allowed to be mixed when building decks; either your deck consists of
>ENTIRLY SABBAT cards or any of the previously printed cards/sets

That's almost right. It is quite logical that you can't mix
Sabbat with Cammarilla. Go read a WW book. The Tremere Antitribu
don't report to Vienna, and the Gangrel Antitribu aren't country
bumpkins. Heck, even the Nosferatu of differing beliefs (read
Antitribu) don't share evrything with their Cammarilla brethren.
Building a Antitribu deck is like building a Independent deck.
It means there are now twenty clans, even if some share the same
name. This doesn't mean you can't combine Sabbat with other
expansions. It's not uncommon to see a two or three clan deck
(expecially if the two clans are essentially the same). And
it's not uncommon for Methuselahs to manipulate both sects at
the same time. We're funny that way. ;-)
